```{r}
# Include spatial coordinates for sliding window analysis
data_selected <- data %>% 
  select(cellID, Patient, cellType, CN, path, X_cent, Y_cent)
```

## Create Non-Overlapping Tile Sub-FOVs

```{r}
# Function to create non-overlapping tile sub-FOVs for each path
create_nonoverlapping_tiles <- function(data, target_tiles = 20) {
  # For each FOV (path), create non-overlapping tiles
  data_with_subfovs <- data %>%
    group_by(path) %>%
    group_modify(~ {
      # Get bounding box for this FOV
      x_range <- range(.x$X_cent, na.rm = TRUE)
      y_range <- range(.x$Y_cent, na.rm = TRUE)
      
      x_span <- x_range[2] - x_range[1]
      y_span <- y_range[2] - y_range[1]
      
      # Calculate grid dimensions to get approximately target_tiles
      # Maintain aspect ratio
      n_x <- ceiling(sqrt(target_tiles * x_span / y_span))
      n_y <- ceiling(target_tiles / n_x)
      
      # Calculate tile sizes (non-overlapping)
      tile_x_size <- x_span / n_x
      tile_y_size <- y_span / n_y
      
      # Assign each cell to a tile based on its coordinates
      .x %>%
        mutate(
          tile_x = pmin(floor((X_cent - x_range[1]) / tile_x_size) + 1, n_x),
          tile_y = pmin(floor((Y_cent - y_range[1]) / tile_y_size) + 1, n_y),
          sub_fov = (tile_y - 1) * n_x + tile_x
        ) %>%
        select(-tile_x, -tile_y)
    }) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    # Create unique sub-FOV identifier
    mutate(path_subfov = paste0(path, "_tile", sub_fov))
  
  return(data_with_subfovs)
}

# Create non-overlapping tile sub-FOVs for merged data
data_merged_subfovs <- data_merged %>%
  create_nonoverlapping_tiles(target_tiles = 20)

# Summary of tiles created
subfov_summary <- data_merged_subfovs %>%
  group_by(path, Relapse) %>%
  summarise(n_subfovs = n_distinct(path_subfov), 
            total_cells = n(),
            cells_per_subfov = total_cells / n_subfovs,
            .groups = 'drop')

print(subfov_summary)

# Overall summary
cat("\nOriginal FOVs:", n_distinct(data_merged$path), "\n")
cat("Total tiles created:", n_distinct(data_merged_subfovs$path_subfov), "\n")
cat("Total cells (no duplication):", nrow(data_merged_subfovs), "\n")
cat("Average cells per tile:", mean(subfov_summary$cells_per_subfov), "\n")
```

## Cell Type Enrichment: Relapse vs Non-Relapse (Tile Level Analysis - Non-Overlapping)

```{r}
# Calculate log2 fold enrichment using tiles
celltype_enrichment <- data_merged_subfovs %>%
  group_by(path, cellType, Relapse) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  group_by(cellType, Relapse) %>%
  summarise(mean_n = mean(n), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Relapse, values_from = mean_n) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~replace(., is.na(.), 0))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(cellType), names_to = 'Relapse', values_to = 'n') %>%
  group_by(cellType) %>%
  mutate(total_n = sum(n)) %>%
  mutate(diff = log2((n/total_n) / (first(n)/first(total_n)))) %>%
  filter(Relapse == 'Y')

# Calculate proportions for statistical testing using tiles
celltype_proportions <- data_merged_subfovs %>%
  group_by(path_subfov, Relapse) %>%
  mutate(total_cells = n()) %>%
  group_by(path_subfov, cellType, Relapse, total_cells) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    proportion = count / total_cells,
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  # Rename path_subfov to path for compatibility with power analysis
  rename(path = path_subfov) %>%
  distinct()

# Wilcoxon test on proportions
wilcox_results <- celltype_proportions %>%
  group_by(cellType) %>%
  do(test = wilcox.test(proportion ~ Relapse, data = .)) %>%
  mutate(
    p_value = test$p.value,
    p_text = case_when(
      p_value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_value < 0.01 ~ "**",
      p_value < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ "ns"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(cellType, p_value, p_text)

# Merge enrichment with p-values
celltype_plot_data <- celltype_enrichment %>%
  left_join(wilcox_results, by = "cellType")

# Barplot
ggplot(celltype_plot_data, aes(x = reorder(cellType, diff), y = diff)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(aes(label = p_text), vjust = ifelse(celltype_plot_data$diff > 0, -0.5, 1.5), size = 5) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = 0, ymin = 0, xmax = Inf, ymax = Inf), fill = 'darkorange2', alpha = 0.02) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = 0, ymin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymax = 0), fill = 'lightsteelblue', alpha = 0.02) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Cell Type Enrichment (Relapse+/Relapse-) - Tile Level (Non-Overlapping)",
       x = "Cell Type",
       y = "Log2 Fold Enrichment",
       caption = "Wilcoxon test on proportions: * p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001, ns = not significant") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))+
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-1.2, 1.2))

# Print statistics table
print(wilcox_results)
```

## Empirical Power Analysis for Cell Types (Tile Level Simulation)

**Purpose:** To evaluate whether the current dataset with non-overlapping tiles (38 original FOVs × ~20 tiles per FOV ≈ 760 tiles) provides sufficient statistical power and to determine the robustness of the relapse vs. non-relapse differences.

**Method:** This section performs a stratified subsampling analysis using the non-overlapping tiles created above. Each tile is independent (no shared cells), which satisfies statistical independence assumptions. At each iteration, a fixed number of tiles is randomly dropped from EACH relapse group (both relapse and non-relapse). The analysis tests dropping different numbers of tiles to assess how robust the statistical findings are. A Wilcoxon rank-sum test is computed for each cell type. Empirical power is defined as the proportion of iterations where p < 0.05, reflecting the probability of detecting a significant difference under the current data distribution.

This simulation-based (empirical) power analysis has been used in previous spatial and single-cell studies, where analytical power formulas are not applicable due to spatial correlation and hierarchical sampling structures (see Gut et al., Nat Methods 2023; Baker et al., Power analysis for spatial omics).

```{r, warning=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
# Function: stratified downsampling by dropping fixed number of tiles
run_subsampling_power_ct <- function(data, n_drop = 1, n_iter = 200) {
  # data: data frame with columns path, Relapse, cellType, proportion
  # n_drop: number of tiles to drop from EACH relapse group
  # n_iter: number of random subsampling iterations
  
  all_celltypes <- unique(data$cellType)
  
  set.seed(123)
  map_dfr(seq_len(n_iter), function(i) {
    # Drop n_drop tiles from each relapse group
    path_by_relapse <- data %>%
      distinct(path, Relapse)
    
    sampled_paths <- path_by_relapse %>%
      group_by(Relapse) %>%
      group_split() %>%
      map_dfr(function(group_data) {
        n_total <- nrow(group_data)
        n_keep <- max(1, n_total - n_drop)
        group_data %>% slice_sample(n = n_keep, replace = FALSE)
      }) %>%
      pull(path)
    
    sampled <- data %>% filter(path %in% sampled_paths)
    
    # Compute Wilcoxon tests per cell type
    res <- map_dfr(all_celltypes, function(ct) {
      ct_data <- sampled %>% filter(cellType == ct)
      # Check if we have data for both relapse groups
      if (nrow(ct_data) < 2 || length(unique(ct_data$Relapse)) < 2) {
        tibble(cellType = ct, p_value = NA_real_)
      } else {
        wt <- tryCatch(wilcox.test(proportion ~ Relapse, data = ct_data),
                       error = function(e) NULL)
        tibble(cellType = ct, p_value = if (is.null(wt)) NA_real_ else wt$p.value)
      }
    }) %>%
      mutate(iter = i, n_drop = n_drop)
    
    return(res)
  })
}

# Run subsampling analysis by dropping 1 to 500 tiles (by 50) from each group
n_drops <- seq(from= 1, to = 500, by =50)
downsample_results_ct <- map_dfr(n_drops, ~run_subsampling_power_ct(celltype_proportions, n_drop = .x, n_iter = 200))

# Summarize empirical power and stability with 95% CI
empirical_power_summary_ct <- downsample_results_ct %>%
  group_by(cellType, n_drop) %>%
  summarise(
    n_tests = sum(!is.na(p_value)),
    n_significant = sum(p_value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    empirical_power = mean(p_value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_logp = median(-log10(p_value), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # 95% CI using binomial proportion (Wilson score interval)
    ci_lower = pmax(0, empirical_power - 1.96 * sqrt(empirical_power * (1 - empirical_power) / n_tests)),
    ci_upper = pmin(1, empirical_power + 1.96 * sqrt(empirical_power * (1 - empirical_power) / n_tests))
  )

# Visualization - separate plot for each cell type with 95% CI
ggplot(empirical_power_summary_ct, aes(x = n_drop, y = empirical_power)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1.1) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 2.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.8, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = n_drops) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  facet_wrap(~ cellType, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Empirical Power for Cell Types: Dropping Tiles from Each Relapse Group",
       subtitle = "Each panel shows the probability (empirical power) of obtaining p < 0.05 for a given cell type. Shaded area = 95% CI. Red dashed line = 80% power threshold.",
       x = "Number of Tiles Dropped from Each Group",
       y = "Empirical Power (p < 0.05)",
       caption = "Simulation-based power analysis (200 iterations per drop level). Equal numbers of tiles dropped from relapse and non-relapse groups.") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "lightblue"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))

# Print summary table
print(empirical_power_summary_ct)
```

**Interpretation:**

- Empirical power represents the proportion of resampling iterations where the Wilcoxon test detects a significant difference (p < 0.05). It quantifies the stability and reproducibility of the observed relapse vs. non-relapse differences under reduced sampling.
- A stable empirical power (≥0.8) when dropping small numbers of tiles indicates that the non-overlapping tile approach with ~760 tiles provides sufficient data for robust inference.
- The power curve shows how statistical power degrades as more tiles are dropped from each group, helping identify the robustness of the detected relapse-associated differences.
- Using non-overlapping tiles increases sample size while maintaining statistical independence (no pseudo-replication), providing more power compared to using only 38 original FOVs.

## Empirical Power Analysis for Cell Neighborhoods (Tile Level Simulation)

**Purpose:** Similar to the cell type analysis above, this section evaluates the statistical power for detecting relapse vs. non-relapse differences in cell neighborhood (CN) composition across the non-overlapping tiles.

**Method:** Stratified subsampling analysis where a fixed number of tiles is randomly dropped from EACH relapse group (both relapse and non-relapse), followed by Wilcoxon rank-sum testing for each cell neighborhood.

```{r, warning=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
# Function: stratified downsampling by dropping fixed number of tiles for CN
run_subsampling_power_cn <- function(data, n_drop = 1, n_iter = 200) {
  # data: data frame with columns path, Relapse, CN, proportion
  # n_drop: number of tiles to drop from EACH relapse group
  # n_iter: number of random subsampling iterations
  
  # Get all unique cell neighborhoods to ensure they are all tested
  all_cns <- unique(data$CN)
  
  set.seed(123)
  map_dfr(seq_len(n_iter), function(i) {
    
    # Drop n_drop tiles from each relapse group
    path_by_relapse <- data %>%
      distinct(path, Relapse)
    
    sampled_paths <- path_by_relapse %>%
      group_by(Relapse) %>%
      group_split() %>%
      map_dfr(function(group_data) {
        n_total <- nrow(group_data)
        n_keep <- max(1, n_total - n_drop)
        group_data %>% slice_sample(n = n_keep, replace = FALSE)
      }) %>%
      pull(path)
    
    sampled <- data %>% filter(path %in% sampled_paths)
    
    # Compute Wilcoxon tests per CN
    # Ensure all CNs are represented in results
    res <- map_dfr(all_cns, function(cn) {
      cn_data <- sampled %>% filter(CN == cn)
      # Check if we have data for both relapse groups
      if (nrow(cn_data) < 2 || length(unique(cn_data$Relapse)) < 2) {
        tibble(CN = cn, p_value = NA_real_)
      } else {
        wt <- tryCatch(wilcox.test(proportion ~ Relapse, data = cn_data),
                       error = function(e) NULL)
        tibble(CN = cn, p_value = if (is.null(wt)) NA_real_ else wt$p.value)
      }
    }) %>%
      mutate(iter = i, n_drop = n_drop)
    
    return(res)
  })
}

# Run subsampling analysis by dropping 1 to 500 tiles (by 50) from each group
downsample_results_cn <- map_dfr(n_drops, ~run_subsampling_power_cn(cn_proportions, n_drop = .x, n_iter = 200))

# Summarize empirical power and stability with 95% CI
empirical_power_summary_cn <- downsample_results_cn %>%
  group_by(CN, n_drop) %>%
  summarise(
    n_tests = sum(!is.na(p_value)),
    n_significant = sum(p_value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    empirical_power = mean(p_value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_logp = median(-log10(p_value), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # 95% CI using binomial proportion (Wilson score interval)
    ci_lower = pmax(0, empirical_power - 1.96 * sqrt(empirical_power * (1 - empirical_power) / n_tests)),
    ci_upper = pmin(1, empirical_power + 1.96 * sqrt(empirical_power * (1 - empirical_power) / n_tests))
  )

# Visualization - separate plot for each cell neighborhood with 95% CI
ggplot(empirical_power_summary_cn, aes(x = n_drop, y = empirical_power)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), fill = "coral", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(color = "coral", size = 1.1) +
  geom_point(color = "coral", size = 2.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.8, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = n_drops) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  facet_wrap(~ CN, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Empirical Power for Cell Neighborhoods: Dropping Tiles from Each Relapse Group",
       subtitle = "Each panel shows the probability (empirical power) of obtaining p < 0.05 for a given cell neighborhood. Shaded area = 95% CI. Red dashed line = 80% power threshold.",
       x = "Number of Tiles Dropped from Each Group",
       y = "Empirical Power (p < 0.05)",
       caption = "Simulation-based power analysis (200 iterations per drop level). Equal numbers of tiles dropped from relapse and non-relapse groups.") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "lightcoral"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))w i

# Print summary table
print(empirical_power_summary_cn)
```

**Interpretation:**

- Empirical power for cell neighborhoods quantifies how robustly we can detect relapse-associated spatial organization patterns under varying sample sizes.
- Cell neighborhoods with consistently high empirical power (≥0.8) when dropping small numbers of tiles represent stable and reproducible spatial features associated with relapse status.
- The power curve for each neighborhood reveals its robustness, showing how sensitive the statistical inference is to the removal of tiles from the dataset.
- The non-overlapping tile approach with ~760 tiles provides higher resolution and more statistical power for detecting spatial patterns compared to 38 original FOVs, while maintaining proper statistical independence.
